title: customer-sigma-incident-timeline-scratchpad
content:
Context:
Customer: customer-sigma (prod org id: sigma-prod-18)
Reported: intermittent 500s and garbled completions on /v1/generate route starting ~2026-02-09 23:50 UTC.
Impact: ~40% of requests from their frontend returned truncated responses or HTTP 500. Time window ~23:50–02:10 UTC.

High-level hypothesis (so far):
- Deploy of redwood-v0.9.1-8bit happened 2026-02-09 22:30 UTC to the eu-west-1 pool. Suspect quantization variant introduced a KV-cache alignment bug or kernel mismatch under certain prompt lengths.
- Secondary: autoscaling/cold-start path hits incompatible model variant transiently.

Timeline (raw breadcrumbs):
2026-02-09 22:30 UTC - deploy redwood-v0.9.1-8bit to eu-west-1 pool (release-engineering tag).
2026-02-09 23:47 UTC - first alert: spike in 5xx for route /v1/generate from sigma-prod -> alert SRE Pager (see slack thread).
2026-02-09 23:50–00:15 UTC - intermittent 500s, increased latency. Customer support ticket opened.
2026-02-10 00:05 UTC - replicated locally on staging by running long prefix prompts (30–80 tokens) against same model binary.
2026-02-10 00:18 UTC - patch candidate: revert to redwood-v0.9.0 on a small canary group; errors drop on canary.
2026-02-10 00:30 UTC - rolled back redwood-v0.9.1-8bit for sigma-prod; customer reports traffic normalized by 00:55 UTC.

Commands run / notes (interactive debugging):
$ kubectl -n inference logs deploy/redwood-runtime-eu-west-1 --since=2h | grep SIGMA_ORG_ID
...
2026-02-09T23:50:07Z ERROR runtime::request_handler - client_id=sigma-prod request_id=abc123 status=500 err="KV cache length mismatch: expected 512 got 496"

Repro (staging):
- Ran load.sh (short) with prompt lengths 16/32/64, concurrency 6, model redwood-v0.9.1-8bit. Fail rate ~28% when prefix length crosses 40 tokens.

Key error snippets:
"RuntimeError: KV cache length mismatch: expected 512 got 496"
"Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/workspace/runtime/serve.py\", line 412, in handle_request
    out = model.generate(...)
  File \"/opt/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/runtime.py\", line 233, in generate
    raise RuntimeError(\"KV cache length mismatch: expected %d got %d\" % (expected, got))
RuntimeError: KV cache length mismatch: expected 512 got 496"

grpc error observed on some clients: "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed" but correlation incomplete (could be client side/backpressure).

Notes on resource errors (not root cause):
- GPU memory usage peaked but did not hit OOM in most traces; occasional CUDA OOM in older hosts, fixed by restart.

Hypotheses to test next:
- Alignment bug in quantized kernel for attention leading to wrong KV sizing for certain sequence lengths (primary).
- Model metadata mismatch: model artifact claims kv-size 512 but binary compiled kernels expect different stride for 8-bit variant (secondary).
- Request routing mixing 8bit and fp16 variants under same session id (less likely but check routing logs).

Immediate action items (for followup):
- [ ] Collect more logs from eu-west-1 nodes between 23:45–00:15 UTC (kubectl logs + /var/log/nvidia-installer). Assigned: Jamal.
- [ ] Run focused repro matrix on staging: prompt lengths 8..96 step 8, concurrency 1/4/8 on redwood-v0.9.1-8bit. Assigned: Linda.
- [ ] Verify model artifact metadata payload (model-card.json) for kv_size/hidden_size/quant config in S3 location s3://redwood-models/redwood-v0.9.1-8bit/. Assigned: Priya.
- [ ] Add assertion in runtime to log request/session id and model variant when KV mismatch occurs (hotfix) and ship to canary. Assigned: eng-serving-runtime.

Draft internal comms (to CS/Account):
Subject: Incident summary (customer-sigma) — 2026-02-09
Hi team,
Quick draft for CS to send to sigma. Please review & shorten:
"Hi Sigma team — We investigated the intermittent 500s observed on 2026-02-09. Root cause appears to be a mismatch between the compiled quantized runtime and the model artifact metadata (KV cache size), introduced in the redwood-v0.9.1-8bit rollout. We rolled back the deployment for your pool at ~00:30 UTC which restored normal traffic.
We are running a detailed repro and will push a canary hotfix with additional logging today. Next update in 3 hours or sooner if we have a fix. Apologies for the disruption and we appreciate your patience. — Linda (SRE)"

Open questions / followups:
- Do we have any customers still on v0.9.1-8bit in eu-west-1 that we haven't rolled back? (check billing/usage).
- Is there a CI gate missing that should have caught kv-size mismatch for quant variants?

References:
- Jira: JIRA-SIGMA-4821
- Slack thread: #incident-sigma (link above)
- Canaries: canary pool id: canary-eu-029

Next scheduled sync: 2026-02-10 09:00 UTC with release eng, runtime, and CS to finalize external comms.

Scratchpad notes (freeform):
- observed that when requests include function-call payloads (tooling enabled) failure rate rises — maybe additional key/value per token for tool-call metadata?
- check session affinity header X-Redwood-Session for mixed-variant routing.
- consider temporary mitigation: route sigma to fp16 variant until 8bit fix validated.

-- end of scratchpad --
